entries.title: Search displaces email
entries.quote: Consumers may well change their use of the Internet, with search potentially displacing email as the most used digital application.
entries.subject: Web search
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report. Section title is Hindsight's label; the report's section headings were not read.

entries.title: Digital data volume
entries.quote: it is forecast that approximately 20 exabytes (billion gigabytes) of new digital data will be created in 2006.
entries.subject: Digital data growth
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report. 'it is forecast' may cite an outside forecast.

entries.title: R&D collaboration and offshoring
entries.quote: With global R&D spending expected to top $1 trillion in 2006, companies will be increasingly likely to seek to share their R&D burden with others.
entries.subject: R&D collaboration
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report.

entries.title: Internet regulation
entries.quote: Some governments may move to tax Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services in the same manner as traditional Public Switched telephone Network (PSTN)
entries.subject: Internet regulation (VoIP tax)
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report.

entries.title: Open source
entries.quote: The software world will likely see its dynamics continue to change, as open source becomes a growing threat to the established software business model
entries.subject: Open source software
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the executive summary of the Technology report.

entries.title: Offshoring evolves from option to obligation
entries.quote: Offshoring as a means of minimizing corporate costs and optimizing efficiency will continue to gain in popularity throughout 2006. In some sectors, offshoring may well evolve from an exceptional practice into a prerequisite for survival.
entries.subject: Offshoring
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: The rise and risk of electronic education
entries.quote: During the year, a growing number of schools in developed countries are likely to install digital whiteboards, such that by 2010 every classroom in developed countries is expected to have one
entries.metric: share of classrooms in developed countries with a digital whiteboard
entries.subject: Interactive whiteboards
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. 'Is expected' cites an outside source (footnote 25).

entries.title: Technology humanizes technology
entries.quote: In 2006, advances in key technology areas – processing and storage – will likely enable significant improvements to the interface between people and machines
entries.subject: Human-computer interfaces
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. The report names speech recognition and voice synthesis.

entries.title: Connectivity transforms the device into a service
entries.quote: 2006 will see the launch of a widening range of devices, from cameras to cars, that have the ability and necessary connectivity to be remotely upgraded, updated, maintained and even generate additional revenue.
entries.subject: Over-the-air device updates
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: The digital divide deepens
entries.quote: The digital divide – that is the gap between those who have digital technology and those who do not – is likely to deepen in a number of directions during 2006.
entries.subject: Digital divide
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report.

entries.title: Life changing technology will likely be the most profitable
entries.quote: However the technology-based products and services with the greatest impact on the bottom line will likely be those that permanently change common human behaviors.
entries.subject: Technology business models
entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. Framing rather than a testable forecast.

entries.title: The digital music revolution has only just started
entries.quote: By the end of the year, music distributed in purely digital form is likely to account for roughly 20 percent of total music revenues, with eight percent expected to come from legal downloads and 12 percent from ring tones

entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. 'The latter' is flat panel televisions (as printed, the sentence compares flat panel and CRT).

entries.note: Read from the Internet Archive copy of the Deloitte PDF on deloitte.com/dtt/. Rank is the chapter order in the report. Also: in some media companies up to 50 percent of staff in some divisions may be made redundant.

notes: 5th edition by count from 2002. Series title 'TMT Trends: Predictions, 2006', published as separate Technology, Media and Telecommunications reports. Only the executive summary of the Technology report was read (Mondaq). Entries are summary-level statements, not the report's headline predictions; labels are Hindsight's. Internet Archive retry (2026-10-02): all three reports read in full from deloitte.com/dtt/ copies on archive.org (each states ten predictions). Technology chapters 1, 2, 5 and 6 correspond to the existing summary entries (search; R&D collaboration; open source; Internet regulation, chapter 'The Internet loses its amateur status'; the 20 exabyte figure is in the search chapter), so only Technology chapters 3, 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10 were appended (entries 6 to 11), then Media 1 to 10 (12 to 21) and Telecommunications 1 to 10 (22 to 31). Appended entries carry the report's chapter headline as title and the chapter number as rank.
